ApplicationSpec.description:
What the application runs, and how its environments and previews deploy
it.

environments.description:
Declares the environment `<environment>` and how it deploys, for at
most 64 environments.

exports.description:
Services of this application that other applications may reach, at
most 64.

imports.description: Services of other applications this application reaches, at most 64.

jobs.description:
Containers that run to completion during each deployment, such as
database migrations, at most 16. They run in the order listed.

oneOf.description:
The Git repository each deployment reads the manifest from. Without
it, deployments use the saved manifest. A manifest read from the
repository can't change it: its own `spec.manifest` is ignored.
Settings shared by every preview.

routes.description:
HTTP routes to the services, at most 64. They take effect when an
environment deploys them.

secrets.description: Secrets piqueld generates a value for in each environment, at most 64.

variables.description:
Default value of the variable `<variable>`, referenced as
`${{ vars.<variable> }}`. An environment's or the previews' own value
replaces it. Variable names start with a letter or `_`, use letters,
digits, `_` or `-`, and are at most 63 bytes. Each table of variables
holds at most 128.

volumes.description: Named volumes the services mount, at most 64.

Build.description: How to build a Git source's image.

oneOf.description: Build the image with Docker Buildx, from a Dockerfile.

args.description:
The value of the build argument `<name>`, passed with
`--build-arg`. Docker records it in the image's metadata, so pass
sensitive values as secrets instead. Build arguments total at most
256 KiB.

oneOf.description: Build context directory, relative to the repository root.

dockerfile.description: Path of the Dockerfile, relative to the repository root.

oneOf.description:
Stage of a multi-stage Dockerfile to build. By default, the final
stage.

EnvironmentConfig.description:
Declares an environment and where it deploys from. Without
`promote_from`, the environment builds its own manifest: the saved one, or
a branch of the `spec.manifest` repository. A block that sets none of
`branch`, `commit`, `promote_from` and `sync` leaves an existing
environment's source as it is.

branch.description:
Branch of the manifest repository the environment deploys. By
default, the branch `spec.manifest` names. Needs `spec.manifest`.

commit.description:
Full commit the environment deploys instead of its branch's head.
Without `branch`, by default the commit `spec.manifest` pins. Needs
`spec.manifest`, and excludes `sync`.

promote_from.description:
Another environment whose releases this one receives with
`piquelctl env promote`, instead of building. It excludes `branch`,
`commit` and `sync`, and can't lead back to this environment.

sync.description:
Whether pushes to the environment's branch deploy it while
`spec.manifest.sync` is on. Off when unset. `true` needs
`spec.manifest`.

variables.description:
The environment's value of the variable `<variable>`. It replaces the
`[spec.variables]` default, or declares a variable without one.

oneOf.description:
The strictest visibility the environment's routes get. `public`
restricts nothing; `private` keeps every route on the tailnet.

Export.description:
A service of this application that other applications may reach over a
private link, as `<service>.<application>`.

applications.description:
Applications whose environments may import the service: at least one,
at most 64, each listed once.

previews.description: Whether previews of those applications may import the service too.

service.description: Service of this application to export, at most once.

FileMode.description:
Octal file permissions from `0000` to `0777`, written as text such as
`"0444"` or `"644"`.

FileSource.description: Where a file's content comes from.

oneOf.description:
Path of a UTF-8 text file in the manifest's repository, relative to
its root, read at the commit the manifest was read from. Only
repository-backed applications can use it.

path.description:
Path of a UTF-8 text file in the manifest's repository, relative to
its root, read at the commit the manifest was read from. Only
repository-backed applications can use it.

oneOf.description: The file's content, inline.

GitRepository.description:
A Git repository and the revision to check out. Git uses the host's
credentials.

branch.description: Branch whose head is checked out when no commit is set.

commit.description: Full commit hash to check out instead of the branch's head.

url.description:
Clone URL or local path of the repository. It can't contain
credentials.

HealthCheck.description: How Docker checks that a service's containers are healthy.

oneOf.description:
Send an HTTP `GET` to a port of the container. A 2xx or 3xx status
passes. The image needs nothing for it.
Seconds between checks, from 1 to 3,600.
Absolute HTTP path to request.

port.description: Container port to request, from 1 to 65535.

oneOf.description:
Consecutive failed checks that make a container unhealthy, from 1
to 100.

Seconds after a container starts during which failed checks don't
count, up to 3,600.
Seconds a check may take before it fails, from 1 to the interval.
Run a command in the container, without a shell. Exit code 0 passes.

command.description: Command and arguments to run. It can't be empty.

oneOf.description: Seconds between checks, from 1 to 3,600.

Consecutive failed checks that make a container unhealthy, from 1
to 100.

Seconds after a container starts during which failed checks don't
count, up to 3,600.
Seconds a check may take before it fails, from 1 to the interval.

Import.description:
A service of another application this application reaches over a private
link, as `<service>.<application>`.

application.description: Application exporting the service. It may be this application.

oneOf.description:
Environment of that application to reach. By default, the one named
like the importing environment. It may reference variables, so
previews can reach e.g. `staging`.

service.description: Service that application exports, imported at most once.

Job.description:
A container that runs to completion during each deployment, such as a
database migration.

command.description:
Command the job runs, instead of its service's command and arguments.
It can't be empty.

environment.description:
The environment variable `<name>` of the job's container only, in
addition to its service's. A name the service also sets is an error.

name.description: Name of the job, unique in the application.

run.description:
When the job runs. `before-rollout` runs it after every source is
prepared, before the services roll out.

secrets.description:
Secrets only the job's container mounts, in addition to its service's.
A target the service already uses is an error.

service.description:
Service whose image, environment, secrets, volumes, resource limits
and network the job reuses. The job also waits for the service's
`depends_on`.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the job may run before the deployment fails, from 1 to 86,400.

oneOf.description:
How the job mounts its service's volumes. `read-only` mounts every
volume read-only, so the job runs beside the services. `exclusive`
keeps the writable volumes writable, and stops every service mounting
them while the job runs.

JobRun.description: Deployment point at which a job runs.

JobVolumeAccess.description: How a job may use the volumes its service mounts.

ManifestRepository.description: The literal `"self"`, selecting the manifest's own repository.

name.description:
Name of the application. A manifest with another name applies to
another application, so rename one with `piquelctl app rename`.

Mount.description: A volume mounted into a service's containers.

read_only.description:
Whether the containers mount the volume read-only. A writable mount
makes rollouts stop the old container before starting its
replacement.

target.description:
Absolute path of the mount in the container, unique in the service.
It can't be `/run/piqueld/probe` or `/run/piqueld/telemetry`, or a
path inside them.

variables.description:
The previews' value of the variable `<variable>`. It replaces the
`[spec.variables]` default, or declares a variable without one.

oneOf.description:
The strictest visibility preview routes get. `private` keeps every
route on the tailnet; `public` restricts nothing.

Redirect.description: A redirect the gateway answers with.

preserve_path.description: Whether to append the request's path and query to `to`.

status.description: HTTP status of the redirect: 301, 302, 303, 307 or 308.

to.description:
Absolute `http` or `https` URL to redirect to, with a lowercase
hostname and no query or fragment. It can't target a hostname the
route serves.

RepositoryManifest.description: The Git repository and file each deployment reads the manifest from.

path.description:
Path of the TOML or JSON manifest file, relative to the repository
root.

repository.description:
The repository holding the manifest, and the branch environments
deploy by default.

oneOf.description: Whether pushes to the repository deploy environments and previews.

RepositorySync.description:
Whether pushes to the manifest repository deploy. It applies to every
preview, and to every environment that opted in and follows a branch
without a pinned commit.

oneOf.description: Deploy only when asked.
List the repository's branch heads every `interval_seconds`.
List the branch heads when GitHub reports a push.

ResourceLimits.description:
CPU and memory limits of each of a service's containers. Set at least
one.

oneOf.description:
CPU limit in thousandths of a CPU, from 1 to 1,048,576: `500` is half
a CPU.
Memory limit in bytes, greater than zero.

Rollout.description:
How Docker replaces a service's containers during a deployment, one at a
time. An empty block keeps the defaults.

oneOf.description:
Seconds Docker watches each new container for failure before it
replaces the next one, from 1 to 3,600. 30 when unset.

`stop-first` stops the old container before starting its replacement,
with a short downtime. `start-first` starts the replacement first, so
both briefly run side by side. When unset, `stop-first` if the service
mounts a volume writable or receives telemetry, `start-first`
otherwise.

Route.description:
An HTTP route: requests for a hostname go to a service, or get a
redirect. A route sets either `service` and `port`, or `redirect`.

hostname.description:
Hostname the route serves, such as `notes.example.com`, unique in the
application. A wildcard such as `*.example.com` serves every name one
label below `example.com` that no exact route claims.

name.description:
Name that selects the route in every environment and preview, e.g.
`piquelctl env url --route web`. It is unique in the application and
can't reference variables.

port.description: Port the service serves HTTP on, from 1 to 65535. Needs `service`.

oneOf.description: Redirect the gateway answers with, instead of a service.

service.description: Service of this application that receives the requests. Needs `port`.

oneOf.description:
Who may connect: `public` for the internet, or `private` for the
tailnet only. The environment's or the previews' visibility can make
it stricter, never looser.

SecretDeclaration.description:
A secret whose value piqueld generates for each environment when one of
its deployments first needs it. A generated value is never replaced, and
never shared with another environment.

name.description:
Name of the secret, unique in the application. It can't reference
variables.

SecretEncoding.description: Text encoding of generated random bytes.

SecretGenerator.description: How piqueld generates a secret's value.

oneOf.description: Random bytes from the operating system, encoded as text.

bytes.description: Number of random bytes before encoding, from 16 to 512.

oneOf.description:
Text encoding of the bytes: lowercase `hex`, or unpadded
`base64url`.
An RSA private key, in PKCS#8 PEM.

bits.description: Size of the key in bits: 2048, 3072 or 4096.

SecretMount.description:
A secret mounted as a file. A name `spec.secrets` declares mounts the
environment's generated value; any other name mounts a value from the
application's secret store.

name.description:
Name of the secret. It may reference variables, so each environment
can mount its own stored secret, e.g. `${{ vars.stripe_key }}`.

target.description:
Absolute path of the file under `/run/secrets/`, unique in the
service.

Service.description: A service: containers running one image, kept at their replica count.

arguments.description:
Arguments that replace the image's default arguments, at most 128
elements of 4,096 bytes each.

command.description:
Command that replaces the image's entrypoint, at most 128 elements of
4,096 bytes each. When empty, the image's entrypoint runs.

depends_on.description:
Services of this application that must be running and healthy before
this one rolls out, each listed once.

environment.description:
The environment variable `<name>` of the service's containers. Names
use letters, digits and `_`, don't start with a digit, and are at most
255 bytes. Values are at most 65,536 bytes. At most 256 variables;
`PIQUELD_INGRESS_PROXIES` is reserved.

files.description:
Read-only files mounted into the containers, at most 32. Their
contents are never rendered with variables. An application's files
total at most 2 MiB.

oneOf.description:
How Docker checks that a container is healthy. Rollouts and the
services depending on this one wait until it passes.

mounts.description: Volumes mounted into the containers, at most 32.

name.description:
Name of the service, unique in the application. The application's
other services reach it by this name.

receives_telemetry.description:
Whether the service receives the daemon's traces, metrics and logs,
on a socket in `/run/piqueld/telemetry`, once its environment is
granted telemetry. At most one service of an application receives
telemetry, with one replica.

oneOf.description: Number of containers, from 1 to 100.
CPU and memory limits of each container.

rollout.description: How Docker replaces the service's containers on each deployment.

secrets.description: Secrets mounted as files, at most 64.

source.description:
Where the service's image comes from: a prebuilt image, or a Git
build.

allOf.description: Where the file's content comes from.

oneOf.description:
Octal permissions, from `"0000"` to `"0777"`. The file is owned by
root.

target.description:
Absolute path of the file in the container, unique among the
service's mount, secret and file targets. It can't be in
`/run/secrets` or `/run/piqueld`.

ServiceFile.description:
A read-only file mounted into a service's containers, from exactly one
source: `path` in the manifest's repository, or inline `content`. Its
content can't be empty, and is at most 500 KiB.

Source.description: Where a service's image comes from.

oneOf.description: Pull a prebuilt image from a registry.

image.description:
Image reference, such as `ghcr.io/example/notes:1.4.0`, with an
optional tag or digest. It can't contain a URL scheme or
credentials.

oneOf.description: Build the image from a Git repository.

repository.description:
Repository to build: `"self"` for the manifest's own repository,
at the commit the manifest was read from, or a table naming
another one. `"self"` needs `spec.manifest`.

SourceRepository.description: The repository a Git build source checks out.

oneOf.description:
`"self"`: the application's manifest repository, at the exact commit its
manifest was read from, so one deployment builds from one revision.
Another repository, and the revision to build.

Template.description:
Text that may contain `${{ namespace.name }}` references, with optional
whitespace inside the braces. `$${{` writes a literal `${{`; `${VAR}` and
`$VAR` are ordinary text, left for shells and applications to expand.

```text
"${{ vars.domain }}"       -> the value of `domain`
"api.${{vars.domain}}"     -> "api." followed by the value of `domain`
"$${{ vars.domain }}"      -> "${{ vars.domain }}", literally
```

TypedTemplate.description:
A template in a setting of another type, such as an integer: text
containing a `${{` reference. A template that is exactly one reference
takes the variable's own value, which must have the setting's type;
strings are never parsed into numbers.

Typed_RolloutOrder.description:
A value written directly, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference takes the variable's own value;
any other template renders to text. The value must have the setting's
type: strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description:
Whether Docker stops the old container before or after starting its
replacement.
A value rendered from variables.

Typed_u16.description:
A value written directly, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference takes the variable's own value;
any other template renders to text. The value must have the setting's
type: strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: A value rendered from variables.

Typed_u32.description:
A value written directly, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference takes the variable's own value;
any other template renders to text. The value must have the setting's
type: strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: A value rendered from variables.

Typed_u64.description:
A value written directly, or a template rendered for each environment.

A template that is exactly one reference takes the variable's own value;
any other template renders to text. The value must have the setting's
type: strings are never parsed into numbers.

oneOf.description: A value rendered from variables.

Variable.description:
A variable's value: a string, an integer or a boolean. A string may
reference system variables, such as `${{ env.name }}`, but not other
variables.

oneOf.description: A boolean.
A signed 64-bit integer.
Text of at most 65,536 bytes, which may reference system variables.

Visibility.description: Who may connect to a route: everyone, or only tailnet devices.

Volume.description:
A named volume the services mount. Its data is kept across deployments,
and when the application is deleted.

name.description: Name of the volume, unique in the application.

description:
An application: what it runs, and how its environments and previews
deploy it.

kind.description: Kind of resource the manifest describes.

spec.description: What the application runs, and how it deploys.

title: piqueld application manifest
